panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 5 panels (A, B, C, D, E). A: Clinical photograph of the patient's hands showing the classic spatulate right thumb described in the caption and in-text for this FLNB mosaic Larsen syndrome case. B: Radiograph of both hands in the same Larsen syndrome patient showing shortened distal phalanges (radiographic correlate of the spatulate thumb) and carpal abnormalities, as stated in the caption. C: Clinical photograph of both feet showing bilateral spatulate toes and calcaneovalgus foot deformity, recognized skeletal manifestations of Larsen syndrome in this patient. D: Spinal radiograph showing a wedge-shaped T4 vertebral body causing thoracic scoliosis, a recognized spinal manifestation of Larsen syndrome described in the caption and in-text. E: Pelvic radiograph showing narrow iliac wings, shortened femoral necks, and right-sided coxa vara, recognized skeletal findings of Larsen syndrome in this patient.
